messages.author: slotherer
messages.text: How is he even in my war range?

messages.author: Affairs and Order
messages.text:
Hi <@249007223454433292>,

Thanks for reporting this and bringing it up!

**Why this happened previously:**
Under the previous war range calculation (`wars/war_range.py`), war strength factored in standing military units alongside population (`population / 1000 + unit weights`). This allowed players to manipulate their effective strength bracket by purchasing or liquidating military units right before declaring war, enabling declarations against nations that appeared well outside normal brackets.

**The Fix:**
Following the community vote in suggestion thread <#1559231782514335815>, this has been officially resolved and deployed to production:
- **PR #209** (*"Remove standing units from war range scoring"*) has been merged. War strength eligibility is now calculated **strictly from population** (`population / 1000.0`, with the standard 75%–133% range). Standing military units now exclusively determine battle/combat outcomes, but never target eligibility.
- In addition, **PR #211** (*"Prevent building liquidation during active wars"*) was deployed to prevent asset liquidation mid-conflict.

War range is now strictly population-based and cannot be manipulated by buying or selling units. Thank you for your patience and for helping make the system fairer!
